observation.visible_scene: Night view through a window pane covered with numerous water droplets; behind the glass a row of out-of-focus warm amber/orange bokeh circles (fixed positions across the frame) and a faint bluish glow at the far left form a static, dark backdrop.
visible_changes: A bright bluish-white out-of-focus light patch enters at the left edge (around the upper-left of the lower band) and translates diagonally toward the lower-right over the first ~0.5 s, passing through positions near the center-bottom and right-bottom before fading.

In later parts of the clip additional bluish-white bright patches reappear at scattered lower-frame locations and shift between frames, sometimes splitting into two or three glints as the light refracts through different droplets.
The overall brightness of the white/blue patches flickers and swells rather than staying constant.
The orange bokeh circles and the droplet pattern on the glass hold their positions throughout, indicating no camera pan/zoom and no visible dripping flow.
outside_clip_unknowns: The actual source producing the moving white light (e.g. a passing vehicle's headlights) is never in focus or directly visible; only its refracted bokeh is seen.
Whether the diagonal traversal is one source or several, and whether the motion continues past the crop boundaries, cannot be determined.
Any earlier onset of the bright patch before t=0 and its final exit after t=3.2 are outside the segment.
uncertain_details: The exact trajectory of the white light is hard to track frame-to-frame because droplets fragment it into multiple bright spots; the apparent 'jumps' are likely refraction splitting, not discrete object teleportation.
No clear droplet movement is visible, so it is uncertain whether the glass is actively being rained on or merely wet and still.
The faint blue glow at the left edge may be a separate stationary light source or part of the same moving one; its identity is not resolved.
